messages.subject: Problem with generating MSImageSet object
parts:
Hi, 

I have been playing around with the Cardinal package for a while with the demo data. Now, I would like to use of of my own datasets. I have an integer matrix with 19 features (rows) and 10,000 coordinates (columns). I would like to generate a MSImageSet object to proceed further. For this, I am using the following command:
imageObject <- generateImage(intensityData, as = "MSImageSet")

Somehow, R is taking really long to perform this. I haven't been able to generate a MSImageSet object yet. Is there something wrong that I am doing?

Thank you for your help.

Best,
Purva

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Problem with generating MSImageSet object
parts:
Hi Purva,

You don't want to use generateImage(), which is actually the function for generating *simulated* data. The first argument of generateImage() is actually meant to be a pattern of regions to simulate, so you're telling to R to simulate images with probably thousands of distinct regions, which is why it's taking so long.

How did you load "intensityData"? Where did it come from?

The usual way of using your data in Cardinal is to use the readMSIData() function to read your data from an imzML or Analyze file, such as:

mydata <- readMSIData("path/to/file.imzML")

If you loaded your data another way, such as reading it from a text file, you need to use the MSImageSet function to turn it into an MSImageSet:

mydata <- MSImageSet(spectra=intensityData, mz=mzData, coord=coordData)

where you have presumably read "intensityData", "mzData", and "coordData" into R some other way.

Please see ?readMSIData and ?MSImageSet for details on loading your data, or creating an MSImageSet from data you've loaded.

-Kylie

Dear Kylie,

I completely missed seeing that generateImage() was for simulated data.
I am working with some SIMS data which originally was in .itm file format. I wasn't able to parse this file, so I have my features of interest as .txt files. Each text file belongs to a specific m/z and provides intensity values for all the coordinates. I imported these files in R and generated a matrix object called 'intensityData' with dimensions (19,10000).

Many thanks!

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Problem with generating MSImageSet object
parts:
This was a bug in assigning feature names to high-resolution datasets in the last release. It should be fixed in the new release (due next week). Sorry about that.

(If you need the fix this week, you can either install from the developer version of Bioconductor, or use the devtools package to install from Github.)

-Kylie
